requirement: each record must be marked as adopted or

This section evaluates the negative knowledge layer in a con-
trolled same-task retry setting on a scientific-coding bench-
mark. We test whether a structured record of a failed attempt
helps a fresh agent repair the same task without access to
the original conversation. We compare negative-knowledge
retry with direct retry and self-debug baselines, measuring
pass rate and the size of the memory object handed to the
next attempt.

Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Anthropic, 2026) on the deterministic-
evaluation subset of ScienceAgentBench (Chen et al., 2024),
where outcomes are verified by programmatic evaluators.

pling), Self-debug (Chen et al., 2023) (three rounds
of raw failure feedback: each later attempt sees the previ-

Stage 2 tests whether the knowledge bank transfers to three
new mathematical physics sub-tasks in the coupled BKdV
system:Test-Asoliton stability near the m= 0 manifold,
Test-BGaussian wave-packet decomposition into a soliton
train, andTest-CKdV-soliton interaction with a Burgers
bore. We compare four conditions applied on the AutoRe-
search pipeline:Base(no bank),Base+Pos(positive records
only),Base+Neg(negative bank only), andBase+Pos+Neg
(full bank). Each cell is allowed up to three AutoResearch
rounds and is judged by deterministic physics-aware checks;
detailed definitions and settings are in Section C.

evidence.excerpt:
We also test whether the BKdV knowledge bank can help
on a substantially different coupled system, Burgers-NLS
(BNLS) (Dombret et al., 2023). In a three-round AutoRe-
search setting, agents without any bank fail all four BNLS
tasks, while agents given only the BKdV bank solve two
of them. This suggests that the bank is not only task-local
memory: some of its numerical failures, diagnostics, and
method warnings transfer to a different nonlinear PDE sys-
tem and become a useful collective asset for the research
team. Details of the BNLS setup are in Section C.5.

evidence.excerpt:
We introduced a negative knowledge memory layer: a cu-
rator agent writes each failed attempt as a bounded, typed
record into a shared bank, and a downstream research agent
must adopt or reject those records before its next experiment.
On ScienceAgentBench, structured records improve retry
pass rate at lower token cost than raw self-debug; on two
coupled PDE systems, the bank enables cross-task trans-
fer that no-bank baselines fail. Within the limits of small
sample sizes and the models studied, this is a first step to-
ward maintaining negative knowledge as shared epistemic
infrastructure for AI-engaged scientific research.

evidence.excerpt:
ScienceAgentBench (Chen et al., 2024) is a benchmark for evaluating language agents on data-driven scientific discovery
tasks drawn from real scientific workflows. It contains 102 tasks extracted from peer-reviewed scientific publications and
evaluates whether an agent can produce an executable solution for each task. We use its deterministic-evaluation subset of
38 tasks to ensure all reported outcomes are verified by programmatic evaluators.

skeleton with a different wave mechanism is what makes BNLS a stringent transfer target.

combined NLS+BKdV bank; all BNLS sub-agents run on Claude Sonnet 4.6. The NLS bank contains 21 entries curated
from eight BNLS stress tests; the BKdV bank reuses a 30-entry snapshot of the BKdV study's bank (10 positive and 20
negative entries).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcomes are established by external programmatic checks and deterministic physics criteria that do not depend on the curator agent.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Programmatic deterministic evaluators on ScienceAgentBench and physics-based numerical gates (mass drift, boundedness, peak counts) on the PDE tasks.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Curator agents synthesize failed run artifacts into typed schema records specifying failure mechanisms and prescriptive actions.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding improved retry pass rates with smaller memory footprints on ScienceAgentBench (e.g., 36.8% vs 31.6% base retry; 47.4% deep retry vs 44.7% raw self-debug) and cross-task transfer on coupled PDEs are directly supported by the tabular results and trace analyses.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated across two distinct empirical environments: 38 deterministic tasks from ScienceAgentBench and numerical research problems on nonlinear coupled PDE systems (BKdV and BNLS). The outcomes are tracked against sensible baselines using objective deterministic programmatic checks, pass rates, and context memory footprints.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline evaluation relies on external programmatic unit tests and physics-based integration checks that operate independently of the curator agent.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Independent programmatic determinism checks on ScienceAgentBench tasks and explicit numerical simulation criteria (such as mass conservation thresholds and peak amplitude gates) for PDE systems.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Curator agents synthesize failed run artifacts into typed schema records specifying failure mechanisms and prescriptive actions.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss constraints, including small sample sizes on PDE benchmarks, negative transfer risks when transferring across systems with incompatible mathematical properties, and the upfront token cost incurred by the curator pass.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology clearly delineates the roles of the curator and research agents, formalizing a structured schema with controlled vocabularies for failure classification and actionable prescription. Its multi-agent setup decouples attempt execution from failure summarization to mitigate self-assessment bias.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a well-scoped architectural concept backed by a clear implementation schema and solid empirical validation. Deterministic evaluators eliminate subjective scoring bias, and experimental comparisons cleanly isolate the value of structured negative memory against direct retry and raw self-debugging.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces a negative knowledge memory layer for autonomous research workflows, where a curator agent converts failed experimental attempts into bounded, typed records stored in a shared bank that downstream research agents adopt or reject before proposing subsequent experiments.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents a well-scoped architectural concept backed by a clear implementation schema and solid empirical validation. Deterministic evaluators eliminate subjective scoring bias, and experimental comparisons cleanly isolate the value of structured negative memory against direct retry and raw self-debugging.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently discuss constraints, including small sample sizes on PDE benchmarks, negative transfer risks when transferring across systems with incompatible mathematical properties, and the upfront token cost incurred by the curator pass.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
